thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: reserved-capacity pool "ded-pool-6" utilization 98% (reserved GPUs=40/40). Queue depth spike for enterprise tenants detected at 2026-05-03 02:00 UTC. Trigger: pool_util_high. Incident channel auto-created: #incidents-1768001234

maya_oncall: I'm on it. Paging out.

sam_sre: I see huge queue growth on resv pool metrics. `queue_length~520` and avg latency > 3.2s/token. Logging sample attached.

li_capacity: autoscaler attempted 3 scale ups but hit max_replicas=10 for nodegroup ded-pool-6. Looks like policy cap; need manual override.

emily_support: Which customers are impacted? Any P1s?

carlos_custsuccess: NovaHealth is showing 40% of queued requests. They have reserved GPUs here. CC: their AM. I'll open bridge.

maya_oncall: Bridge opened: zoom://redwood.incidents/1768001234. I'm running `kubectl get pods -n ded-pool-6` now.

infra-bot: `kubectl get pods` output: 40/40 pods Running, 12 pods showing OOMKilled evictions last 10m. Node utilization: GPU 100%, mem 92%.

sam_sre: Looks like noisy neighbor: several long-lived batch sessions from tenant "data-ingest-service" holding KV caches. Can we preempt?

li_capacity: We have preemption enabled for low-priority sessions, but those belong to reserved reservations flagged non-preemptible. I can temporarily toggle by updating reservation policy, but need exec privileges and approval.

maya_oncall: Propose: 1) throttle non-enterprise burst (global token bucket), 2) preempt batch jobs labeled `job=backgrounding`, 3) temporarily increase max_replicas to 14 for ded-pool-6 while we stabilize. Anyone object?

emily_support: Throttling non-enterprise may raise API error rates for some customers. Inform Status page and notify support.

carlos_custsuccess: NovaHealth on the bridge, they confirm degraded latency but no hard errors yet. AM requests we prioritize their requests.

sam_sre: Ok I'll run preemption script: `/ops/preempt_lowpri.sh --pool ded-pool-6 --label job=backgrounding` pasting logs:

```
preempt: found 18 candidates, evicting 14
evict: pod data-ingest-77 -> reason=preempted, kube_reason=Evicted
```

maya_oncall: Running scale command now: `infractl scale --pool ded-pool-6 --max 14 --reason "mitigation: night surge"` (will require infra approval)

infra-bot: Approval required from @li_capacity or @ops_admin. li_capacity approved via reaction :white_check_mark:.

li_capacity: Approved. Scaling up nodes, ETA ~4m. Monitor queue.

maya_oncall: Also enabling prefix KV cache flush for largest sessions to free memory: `runtimectl cache flush --pool ded-pool-6 --tenant data-ingest-service --confirm`

sam_sre: After preemption and cache flush, queue dropped to 220 within 2m. Latency down to 1.8s/token. Good signal.

emily_support: Posting status update: "Investigating degraded performance for customers on ded-pool-6; mitigation in progress." Will pin.

carlos_custsuccess: NovaHealth: "Thanks, still seeing lag but much better." They asked for post-incident writeup.

maya_oncall: Root cause quick note: autoscaler blocked by max_replicas config + noisy long-running background jobs from mixed tenant workloads. Reserved reservation policies prevented preemption. We're doing a long-term follow-up.

li_capacity: Followups: 1) adjust autoscaler policy to allow emergency burst beyond commit for short windows 2) add tenant isolation rule to avoid mixed critical+low jobs on same reserved nodes 3) evaluate default max_replicas per pool.

sam_sre: Creating incident ticket INC-2026-176800 in Jira with annotated metrics and logs.

emily_support: What's the timeline for fully restoring to normal? Any risk of reoccurrence tonight?

maya_oncall: Scaling complete, queue stabilized <50, latency ~0.6s/token. I'll keep monitors on for 30m. Reoccurrence possible if another batch job starts; I'll set automated alert to auto-preempt if queue >150 and utilization>95%.

carlos_custsuccess: I'll coordinate with NovaHealth to schedule a review and offer a throughput ramp plan.

infra-bot: Post-mortem checklist created: `/ops/incidents/create_checklist 1768001234`

maya_oncall: Reassigning to Sam for triage and Li for capacity follow-up. I'm wrapping handoff.

sam_sre: Got it. Oncall notes saved. I'll add links to heap profiles and eviction traces.

emily_support: Support runbook updated with customer messaging templates for reserved pool saturation.

maya_oncall: Final: incident cleared, moving to monitoring state. :party-parrot: 

incident-bot: Incident status set to "mitigated" at 1768001475 by maya_oncall.
